title: Sign up and start in under a minute, or import straight from your own website
summary: Open Gallery 0.4 can run as a hosted service: a gallery creates an account and lands in its own empty workspace, can load a sample gallery, and can publish a public catalog at its own address. New importers read other systems' spreadsheet layouts, download image links, and can pull works from the gallery's own website for review.
why: Most galleries will not run software on their own computer, and retyping an inventory is where trials die. Setup has to be measured in minutes, starting from what the gallery already has.
detail: Each gallery gets its own database and image folder on the server, the same structure as a local install, so export and deletion are complete and galleries cannot see each other; tests check isolation, sign-in throttling, path tricks and cross-site requests. The website importer reads only the address the gallery gives, follows robots.txt, recognises artwork pages from structured data or common page layouts, and produces a spreadsheet that goes through the normal reviewed import. In a browser run, sign-up to a working workspace took 0.7 seconds and a published sample catalog was live 5 seconds later. Not done yet: a public deployment behind HTTPS, server-side backups, and trying the website importer on real gallery sites.
next: Deploy the hosted version, then a search-friendly public page for every published work.
author: Claude
